title: The Uniform of the Lower Danube
premise: In 1899, along the flood-prone reaches of the Lower Danube, Sebastian Ravensworth has survived five years as the invisible man: driver, errand-runner, and quiet censor of letters for a network of suffragists hiding from imperial authorities. When the army requisitions the river town and seizes the ledger holding every name his found family has protected, Sebastian is coerced into serving as the officer's courier—the one man who could either destroy them or save them. As evacuation berths on the last steamship dwindle, he discovers the ledger can be forged, but only at the cost of exposing his own long-buried name and the sister he abandoned years ago. In the end, Sebastian trades his invisibility for truth, surrendering himself to the authorities so that his found family—and the sister who never stopped searching for him—board the final ship before the century turns.
about_author: Wendell Amberdale is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing border-town records along the Danube before turning to fiction. He writes historical novels about the people history files under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Reading of Letters
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. We meet him steaming open letters in the suffragists' cellar kitchen, memorizing which silences protect which people, while his found family—widow Ilka, printer's boy Tomas, and Madame Veres—treat him as furniture with a heart. When word arrives that the army is requisitioning the town, Sebastian burns three letters and lies to the group about why. Emotional beat: the comfort of a constructed life beginning to crack.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, with an interlude in Captain Brandt's. The army seizes the town hall and the ledger; Brandt, shrewd and tired, offers Sebastian a bargain—serve as courier and the names stay buried, or refuse and face a tribunal. Sebastian delivers his first censored message under an officer's eyes and realizes Brandt already suspects him. Emotional beat: the vertigo of being seen after years of practiced invisibility.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The steamship Korona arrives with berths for forty; the ledger lists sixty. Sebastian forges passages for his family, then discovers his estranged sister Ana among the refugees at the dock—the name he buried is the name the ledger demands. Brandt corners him with proof of the forgeries and offers a final trade: Sebastian's confession for one extra berth. Emotional beat: the collision of loyalty, guilt, and the arithmetic of survival.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, closing with Ana's letter read aloud. He confesses, giving Brandt the true ledger and himself, and watches from the dock as the Korona pulls away carrying Ilka, Tomas, Madame Veres, and Ana—the sister who finally knows his whole truth. Interrogated but not condemned, he is released into a new century with no name to hide behind and, for the first time, nothing left to censor. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into freedom.
